 Breezy Saturday, Windy Sunday 
 Enjoy a Last Weekend of “Late” Sunsets! 
 WWSB ABC7 Good Morning Suncoast - Weekdays at 6am By Mike Modrick Published : Oct. 24, 2026 at 9:05 AM EDT | Updated : 12 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google SARASOTA, Fla. (WWSB) - The last half of October has been dry. But we are still far above our average rain for Autumn. So far we’re holding at 9.74” of rain for October at SRQ. Since September 1 st we’ve received 21.57”. Eastern Florida has received more rain than we have. One of the wettest spots in the state has been North Miami Beach, with reports up to 37” since September 1 st . 
 Autumn Rain (Autumn Rain) The Suncoast is in for more sunshine, but hold onto your hats—it’s going to be breezy! A strong high-pressure system is building over the northeast and extending down through Florida, while a stationary frontal boundary sits across the Florida Straits. This setup is creating gusty northeast winds that will be our main story through the middle of next week. 
 Sunday turns windier as the system strengthens. Expect sunny skies to continue, but those northeast winds will really pick up, making it feel more energetic outside. Next week stays in the same pattern—mainly dry and windy with northeast winds continuing to blow. 
 TROPICAL OUTLOOK - NEXT 7 DAYS 
 Tropical Outlook (Tropical Outlook) The National Hurricane Center is not expecting any tropical cyclone formation over the next seven days across the North Atlantic, Caribbean Sea, or Gulf of Mexico. The Suncoast remains in good shape with no tropical threats on the horizon.
 🎾 Saturday Sports Forecast – More Wind 
 Remember the sunscreen and watch out for the winds!
 Tennis & Pickleball: Sunny skies and low 80s make for perfect playing conditions. The northeast winds at 10 to 20 mph with gusts over 20 mph could affect ball flight, particularly on outdoor courts. You might notice the wind pushing serves and volleys, so adjust your aim accordingly. It’s a great day to be outside!
 Tee Time Forecast (Tee Time Forecast) Golf: Golfers will love Saturday’s weather. Sunny skies, comfortable temperatures in the low 80s, and those northeast winds could actually help carry your drives. Just be mindful that the breezy conditions might affect your short game around the greens. Overall, good conditions for a round.
 Beach & Boating Forecast Saturday - Rip Current Risk: Moderate Lightning Risk: None 
 Hold on to the beach umbrella! Our windy and dry weather pattern continues.
 🏖️ Saturday Beach Forecast 
 AMI Forecast (AMI Forecast) Saturday brings sunny skies and comfortable low 80s—perfect beach weather. The northeast winds at 15 to 20 mph will keep things lively but not uncomfortable. Surf will be minimal at a foot or less, so it’s ideal for wading and swimming rather than surfing. The moderate rip current risk means swimmers should stay aware and swim near lifeguards, but conditions are generally safe for beach-goers. No thunderstorms are expected, so you can plan your beach day with confidence. It’s a beautiful day to enjoy the sand and water on the Suncoast.
 ⛵ Suncoast Boating Forecast - Small Craft Advisories Saturday to Wednesday Evening
 Boating Forecast (Boating Forecast) Northeast winds will dominate the Suncoast waters over the next several days, creating challenging boating conditions. Advisory-level winds are expected to persist for the next several days, with particularly strong gusts likely on Sunday when gale-force conditions may develop. A gale watch may be needed for portions of the waters on Sunday. Boaters should monitor marine forecasts closely and be prepared for rough seas and strong winds.
 Saturday : Northeast winds around 20 to 25 knots. Bay and inland waters will be rough. Conditions are manageable but require caution and proper preparation.
 Sunday : Northeast winds 20 to 25 knots, increasing to 25 to 30 knots in the afternoon with gale-force gusts likely. Bay and inland waters will be very rough. This is a challenging day for boating—only experienced boaters in well-equipped vessels should venture out, and many may choose to stay ashore.
 Monday : Northeast winds 20 to 25 knots with gusts up to 30 knots. Bay and inland waters remain rough. Conditions are still advisory-level and require careful attention to safety protocols.
 Tuesday : Northeast winds 20 to 25 knots. Bay and inland waters rough. Conditions begin to ease slightly as we move into mid-week, but winds remain strong.
 Boaters should secure loose items, check all safety equipment, and consider postponing non-essential trips until winds decrease mid-week.
